planningRules.rule: Say which of the three kinds this is, and what follows. A person assignment names a custodian and puts the asset on their exit checklist; a room or department assignment names nobody and puts it on no checklist at all — an expensive machine assigned to a department can leave the school with somebody and be caught by nothing (BR-1, BR-5, OQ-2).

Say what the previous assignment was. Assigning ends it rather than adding a second, so this quietly takes the asset away from whoever had it — and where that was a person, the reason belongs on a reassignment (BR-7, BR-10, E1).
Never assign to somebody who has left. The custodian must be an active record, and an asset in a departed person's name is one nobody can be asked about (BR-8, E3).
Always record who authorised it. It is required on every assignment and it is the only name against the movement (BR-3, E4).
Never record a campus move as an ordinary assignment. It is a transfer, and the two mean different things to a group (BR-4, E7).

fields.name: by_person
fields.description: Assets in individual names. These are the ones with a custodian and the ones that appear on an exit checklist (BR-1, BR-5).

fields.name: by_room_or_department
fields.description: Assets with no custodian at all. Nobody answers for these and they appear on nobody's exit checklist — whether a departmental asset should have a custodian is unanswered (BR-1, A5, OQ-2).

fields.description: On the register, assigned to nothing. Registering assigns to nobody and nothing chases the next step (UC-18-07 BR-9, E8).

fields.description: Assets assigned to people serving notice or already gone. An asset assigned to a person is not released by that person leaving, and the exit cannot complete while any remain (BR-5, E8).

planningRules.rule: Separate the assets with a custodian from the ones without. A person assignment names somebody who can be asked; a room or department assignment names nobody, and the school finds that out only when something goes missing (BR-1, A5, OQ-2).
Name anything held by somebody who is leaving. An asset assigned to a person is not released by that person leaving, and the exit cannot complete while any remain (BR-5, E8).
Name the assets nobody has ever been assigned. Registering assigns to nobody and nothing forces an assignment afterwards, so an asset can sit unattributed indefinitely (UC-18-07 BR-9).
Give the days held, and say that nothing acts on them. A laptop held by one person for four years is visible here and triggers nothing anywhere (OQ-4).

planningRules.rule: Give the reasons alongside the movements. A move away from a person carries one and a move away from a room does not, so a history is a mixture of explained and unexplained movements and it is worth saying which is which (BR-10, E6).
Name who authorised each move. That is the whole point of recording it — an asset that moved with nobody's name against the move is one nobody can be asked about (BR-3, E4).
Distinguish a campus transfer from a reassignment in the history. They read the same as movements and mean different things to a group (BR-4).
Name the stretches when it was assigned to nothing. An asset registered and never assigned sat with nobody answering for it, and that period is invisible in a list of holders (BR-1).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing. The record it reads is never deleted (BR-6, E9).

request.text: ye projector kahan kahan raha hai aur kis ne manzoori di thi?
request.gloss: where has this projector been and who authorised the moves?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give each holder in turn with the dates, the days held and the authoriser. Mark which moves carry a reason and which do not — only a move away from a person does, so the two moves between rooms have no explanation recorded at all. Note the four months after registration when it was assigned to nothing.
